topics.flagship-ru-ua: Zelenskyy warned that restrictions on Starshield hamper Kyiv's ability to shoot down Russian drones, threatening Ukraine's energy defenses (4 outlets). Separately, 4 outlets discuss a reported US pitch that would have Ukraine give up Donbas in exchange for a NATO seat, which touches red lines for both Kyiv and Moscow. Single-source reports say Ukrainian strikes hit Nizhnekamsk with a fire reported at a major petrochemical plant, and that three ships were struck by drones in the Black Sea near a Romanian shipping canal, which Romania's prime minister called a violation of international law. Another single-source report says Estonia will close its Russian border in two weeks after a thwarted arson attack on a drone factory that it attributes to Russian military intelligence.
topics.flagship-ir-il: An Israeli air strike killed a senior Hamas military commander in Khan Younis, according to Israel (9 outlets). In Yemen, government forces are withdrawing from the Bab al-Mandeb Strait area to defend their main base in Aden, a major setback for the Saudi-backed campaign against the Houthis (2 outlets). One outlet reports that the Saudi-led coalition intercepted two missiles and two drones over Riyadh. Indonesia and 17 other countries condemned an Israeli strike on Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis, the EU's Kaja Kallas voiced grave concern over Gaza's humanitarian crisis, and Iran says a supertanker carrying 2 million barrels of oil sank in the Gulf. A US Army whistleblower alleges that leaders ignored warnings before an attack on a command post in Kuwait.
topics.T15: The FAA's nationwide ground stop on Friday drew coverage from 8 outlets, mostly political reaction such as Buttigieg's jab at the administration. Microsoft Outlook users reported fresh problems a day after Microsoft declared its global outage over (2 outlets). Other items are minor or general: a magnitude 4.5 earthquake in Khargone, India with no casualties reported, the biggest waves in a decade hitting California beaches, and preparedness and vulnerability studies for India, Srinagar, the Philippines and Malta.
topics.T01: A Myanmar military airstrike on a displacement camp in Rakhine state killed 12 people (2 outlets). In Yemen, Houthi sniper fire and shelling in Taiz reportedly killed a woman and wounded eight civilians, and southern forces are repositioning to defend Aden. Other items are lower-signal: China-linked Panama port extradition, the Philippine National Security Adviser's call for a 2031 South China Sea planning horizon, and a US contractor's guilty plea to spying for Ethiopia.
topics.T02: No standalone humanitarian-crisis stories appear here. The only entry is a pointer to a report on Gazans living in a cemetery, which is covered under the Middle East flagship.
topics.T04: Congo's Ebola outbreak remains out of control six months after it was announced, with more than 11,000 cases recorded and nearly half fatal (4 outlets). The only other item is a single-source India quarantine rule for international arrivals that reads like older COVID-era guidance, so its relevance today is doubtful.
topics.T05: ASEAN has agreed to re-engage Myanmar's sidelined leaders in stages, with restrictions staying until there is meaningful progress on its peace plan (3 outlets). The only other item is a single-source opinion piece on a political crisis in Poland, which offers little detail.
topics.T06: Coverage is sparse and mixed. Items include protests in France with reported turnout of about 106,000, housing protests and arrests in Barcelona, and tens of thousands rallying in Prague against a plan to scrap the public media fee. Retrospective pieces on Tonga's 2006 riots and on historical mass protests are also present. Some of the France items may be older reporting.
topics.T07: The only item is a set of headlines with no independent sources counted, saying Trump, Putin and Xi are expected to hold a trilateral meeting that includes nuclear non-proliferation. It is unverified and no detail is given.
topics.T08: Jordan's State Security Court sentenced three men to death for an October 23 terrorist attack in Hmoud, Karak (4 outlets). Guatemala declared a 30-day state of emergency in two eastern departments over drug-linked violence. Other single-source items cover Nigeria (bandit kidnappings in Kaduna, Tinubu's pledge to rebuild Plateau communities), a political dispute over the Kishtwar SPO deaths in India, and general commentary.
topics.T10: Hegseth's proposed $1.5T Pentagon budget faces hurdles after a Democratic midterm sweep (2 outlets), and 128 countries met in Geneva to try to set limits on lethal autonomous weapons (2 outlets). A Royal Navy Trident submarine returned from the longest deployment at sea for a British vessel. The first permanently stationed F-15EX fighters arrived at Kadena Air Base, and Germany proposed a record €561 billion 2027 budget.
topics.T11: India and Myanmar concluded the harbor phase of IMNEX-26 in Visakhapatnam (2 outlets), and India and Sri Lanka began Mitra Shakti XII, running November 13-26. Kuwait's army concluded Kazma-12, a logistics-focused exercise, and Australian troops tested jungle armour in a joint exercise.
topics.T12: A cyberattack on La Poste subsidiary Maileva, reportedly in mid-September, exposed names and addresses of 22 million people in France (single source). Microsoft Outlook users also reported renewed problems after the global outage was declared over, covered under Disaster / Access Denial.
topics.T13: Coverage is mixed and mostly single-source. Spanish coastguards reportedly rescued 1,488 migrants on 14 boats in the Canary Islands in one day. The US Supreme Court will review a challenge to Trump's 'invasion' executive order on migration, and UK items cover settlement rule changes, a claim that crime-by-foreigners data is being withheld, and a reported military-base migrant camp in Oxfordshire.
topics.T14: The US Embassy in Bahrain issued a security alert advising citizens to prepare for possible armed attacks, flight disruptions and travel delays in the region (single source). No further detail on the threat is given.
topics.T16: Cape Verde held a presidential election in which incumbent Jose Neves was favored against challengers including the country's first woman candidate (3 outlets). Alaska voters reportedly kept ranked choice voting, rejecting a Trump-backed measure to end it. Other items: Melaka's election result strengthening a BN-PN alliance against Anwar, a Bucharest rally for the banned candidate Calin Georgescu, Bulgaria's election, and NZ nurses' claims that Auckland hospital patients could not vote.

bluf: Israel says an air strike killed a senior Hamas military commander in Khan Younis, southern Gaza (9 outlets). Separately, Indonesia and 17 other countries condemned an Israeli strike on Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis. Congo's Ebola outbreak remains out of control six months after it was announced, with more than 11,000 cases recorded and nearly half fatal. Zelenskyy warned that restrictions on Starshield hamper Ukraine's ability to shoot down Russian drones and threaten its energy defenses. In Yemen, government forces are withdrawing from the Bab al-Mandeb Strait area to defend their main base in Aden, a major setback for the Saudi-backed campaign against the Houthis, and one outlet reports the Saudi-led coalition intercepted missiles and drones over Riyadh. A Myanmar military airstrike on a displacement camp in Rakhine state killed 12 people. Romania's prime minister said three ships were struck by drones in the Black Sea near a Romanian shipping canal, calling it a violation of international law; this is a single-source report. The US Embassy in Bahrain reportedly issued a security alert advising citizens to prepare for possible armed attacks, flight disruptions and travel delays.
